issues.description: The UML in the problem statement (and the task text) specifies numberOfInscribedStudents as an int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as a long. This type inconsistency between specification and solution will confuse students about the intended type and may lead to compilation issues when they try to implement methods that assume int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfInscribedStudents consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to use int for numberOfInscribedStudents (and update constructor/getter/setter accordingly) to match the UML, or update the problem statement/UML to specify long and adjust the UML-return types and task text consistently.

issues.description: The constructor in the solution uses a long parameter for numberOfInscribedStudents, while the UML and problem text expect that attribute to be an int. This constructor parameter mismatch will mislead students about the expected signature and types they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter type with the specification. If the UML/design expects int, change the constructor signature and parameter type to int (and adjust the field type). If long is intentional, update the UML and task descriptions to require long instead of int.

issues.description: getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the solution is declared to return int but returns the sum of numberOfGuestStudents (int) and numberOfInscribedStudents (long). Because the attribute is long, the expression is long and cannot be returned as int without a cast — this creates a compile-time type mismatch and confusion about the correct return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the return type and operand types are consistent. Either change numberOfInscribedStudents to int so the method can correctly return an int, or change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long and update the UML/problem statement to reflect the long return type.
